absent: Fair-class bandwidth getters and setter internals behind the delegation
Real-time tree-walk predicates and global schedulability constraints
Shares, weight conversion and clamp handler internals
Extensible-scheduler dispatch, enablement lifecycle and weight hook
MM CID allocation, per-CPU structures and fixup helpers
Cgroup subsystem attach and lifecycle handler internals
Exact numeric values of bandwidth minima, maxima and unlimited sentinel
Statistics counter update paths outside the show handlers

findings.text: Bandwidth query helper reports current period, quota and burst for a group, using live fair-class state when that feature is active and cached extensible-scheduler values otherwise; single-field readers build on it.

Group bandwidth update rejects the root group, rejects values that would overflow microsecond to nanosecond conversion, enforces minimum period and quota floors, caps period above, caps quota and quota plus burst against a global maximum, then delegates to fair-class setter and extensible notifier.
Per-field cgroup writers preserve the two untouched bandwidth parameters while replacing the addressed one, mapping negative quota input to the unlimited marker before invoking the common validator.

Unlimited quota uses an internal sentinel shown as negative one on read and as textual max on the unified interface; unified show prints quota then period while unified write parses that pair and retains burst.
Extensible scheduler exposes bandwidth and idle propagation hooks that forward group changes to an optional scheduler callback and cache values locally; disabled builds provide no-op inline variants.
Extensible-scheduler group updates hold a percpu read guard across scheduler lookup, conditional callback and cached-state store.
Extensible-scheduler callbacks fire only when cgroup support is active, a scheduler is attached, the relevant operation exists, and at least one bandwidth value differs or the idle flag differs.
Real-time bandwidth control exposes setters for runtime and period plus getters for both, converting between microseconds at the cgroup boundary and nanoseconds internally.

Real-time update rejects zero runtime for root, rejects zero period, rejects over-limit non-infinite runtime, and maps negative microsecond input to unlimited while rejecting values that overflow time conversion.

Real-time update checks schedulability under a constraints mutex, then publishes period and runtime under the group runtime lock with interrupts disabled while refreshing each possible CPU queue under its own runtime lock.
Schedulability probe packages target group, period and runtime into a small descriptor and walks the group tree inside a read-side critical section, returning walk status.
Idle control exposes a read returning the group flag and a write path that applies the fair-class transition then notifies the extensible scheduler only on success.

Idle transition is idempotent, rejects root and out-of-range values, marks the group and each per-CPU fair queue, adjusts queued versus idle accounting up the ancestor chain until an already idle ancestor or dequeued entity, then assigns minimum shares when idle and default shares otherwise.
Idle transition holds the shares mutex across the whole operation and acquires each run-queue lock with interrupts saved while mutating that CPU queue and walking its entities.

Legacy and default cgroup file tables bind names to read and write handlers for shares, idle, fair bandwidth triple, statistics, clamps, weight forms and unified max, terminated by an empty entry; subsystem descriptor wires lifecycle, attach, statistics and file tables with early and threaded flags.

Legacy names cover shares, idle, fair period quota burst, stat variants and clamp limits; real-time names are runtime and period with microsecond suffix; default names cover weight, weight nice, idle, max, max burst and clamp limits; several default files exclude root.

Real-time group scheduling is gated by a static key with different defaults per build variant, toggled by a boot parameter accepting only zero or one, with legacy file registration skipped when disabled.
Extra and local statistics reporters emit fair bandwidth counters and throttled or burst times converted to microseconds, producing no output when the bandwidth feature is disabled.

Weight writes enforce cgroup minimum to maximum range and translate to scheduler weight before applying shares and notifying extensible scheduler; nice writes enforce nice range, map through the priority table with speculative-index hardening, then apply and notify with translated weight.
Nice read selects the table entry whose weight is closest to current group weight by scanning increasing priority until distance grows, then converts that index to nice.
Priority to weight and priority to multiplier tables each hold forty entries covering nice minus twenty to plus nineteen, with default priority mapping to weight one thousand twenty four.

Memory context identifier teardown removes the caller from the user set, clears active and transit markers, drops per-CPU ownership on mode change with fixup for remaining users, and for the last user synchronizes pending interrupt and scheduled work after removal; exec entry delegates to the same teardown.

Identifier teardown holds the context mutex across the user-count check, takes the context spin lock with interrupts disabled for list and counter mutation, asserts that lock in the removal helper, and synchronizes work only after locks are released for the final user.

Bandwidth paths defend against time-unit overflow by pre-checking against the maximum divisible by nanoseconds per microsecond; real-time getters use a splitting division helper; group iteration covers every possible CPU.
Idle path warns if a queue idle state is unexpectedly unchanged; identifier exit warns on unexpected per-CPU mode or mismatched memory context.
CPU task dumper prefers a register dump when in hard interrupt on the current CPU with available registers, otherwise attempts a single-CPU backtrace and falls back to task display.
Fair-class idle setter has an enabled variant performing the full transition and a header fallback that immediately reports success without action.
